question: Let \(n\) be the smallest nonprime integer greater than \(1\) with no prime factor less than \(10.\) Then
solution:
The smallest allowed prime factor is \(11\). Since \(n>1\) is not prime, it is composite, so write \(n=ab\) for integers \(a,b>1\).

Both factors must be at least \(11\). Indeed, any integer from \(2\) through \(10\) has a prime divisor among \(2,3,5,7\); if such an integer divided \(n\), that smaller prime would also divide \(n\). Therefore
\[
n=ab\ge11\cdot11=121.
\]
This bound is attained by \(121=11^2\), whose only prime factor is \(11\). Hence the smallest qualifying integer is \(\boxed{121}\), and \(120<121\le130\), choice C.
